__
 
• The quorum to constitute a meeting of the Lok Sabha is one-tenth of the total number of members of the House.
 
• This means that at least 10% of the total membership must be present for the proceedings to be valid.
 
• This rule is designed to ensure that decisions are made with adequate representation from the members.
 
• If at any time during a meeting, the number of members present is less than the quorum, it is the duty of the Speaker to either adjourn the House or to suspend the meeting until the quorum is met.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lok Sabha:**

 
 
• The Lok Sabha is the lower house of India's bicameral Parliament, with members directly elected by the people of India.
 
• It is also known as the House of the People.
 
• The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is 552 members, which includes up to 530 members from the states, up to 20 members from the Union Territories, and not more than 2 members of the Anglo-Indian community nominated by the President of India.
 
 
 
• **Quorum:**
 
 
• The quorum is the minimum number of members required to be present in the House before it can conduct its business.
 
• In the context of the Lok Sabha, the quorum is one-tenth of the total membership of the House.
 
• If the quorum is not met, the Speaker has the authority to adjourn the House or suspend the meeting until the quorum is achieved.
 
 
 
• **Speaker of the Lok Sabha:**
 
 
• The Speaker is the presiding officer of the Lok Sabha, responsible for maintaining order and decorum within the House.
 
• The Speaker is elected from among the members of the Lok Sabha.
 
• The Speaker has the authority to adjourn the House or suspend the meeting if the quorum is not met.
